label: Topology and Differential Geometry
notes: Open the chapter. This is the geometric heart of the foundations: manifolds, tangent spaces, Riemannian metrics, and curvature. The deck follows PDF pages 37 through 50 and explains why curved domains, not flat vectors, are the natural setting for much real-world data in geometric deep learning.

label: Manifolds
notes: Define a smooth manifold as a space locally homeomorphic to Euclidean space with smoothly compatible charts. Atlases and transition maps make calculus coordinate-independent. Examples relevant to GDL include spheres, the rotation group as a manifold, and surfaces approximated by meshes.

label: Tangent Spaces
notes: Introduce the tangent space at a point as the vector space of velocities of curves through that point. The differential of a smooth map acts linearly between tangent spaces. Tangent vectors are where gradients and feature directions live once the domain is curved rather than flat.

label: Riemannian Metrics
notes: Add a Riemannian metric: a smoothly varying inner product on each tangent space. It defines lengths, angles, geodesics, and the volume element. Geodesics generalize straight lines and give the shortest-path distance used to compare points on curved data domains.

label: Curvature
notes: Discuss curvature as the obstruction to a manifold being flat, captured by the Riemann tensor and summarized by sectional and Ricci curvature. Curvature controls how geodesics spread or converge and influences the design and stability of networks operating intrinsically on manifolds.

label: Recap
notes: Close the chapter. Manifolds give curved domains, tangent spaces give local linear structure, Riemannian metrics give length and geodesics, and curvature measures departure from flatness. Chapters 05 and 06 add functional analysis and spectral theory to operate on functions over these spaces.
